paper_title: Low-Energy Supernovae Severely Constrain Radiative Particle Decays
notes: Headline result: red-shaded exclusion region of Fig. 2 (MainPlot.pdf in e-print), for radiative energy deposition E_mantle < 0.1 B and progenitor radius R_* = 5e13 cm (the main reference case; the R_*=3e12 dotted and E<1B thin-solid curves are secondary variants not reported). Coordinates recovered from the red vector fill outline; axis log-calibrated from tick labels (x: 1,10,100 MeV; y: 1e-10..1e-7 GeV^-1). Paper's coupling L = G_agammagamma a E.B equals the canonical g_agamma since F.Ftilde = -4 E.B, so no conversion needed. The exclusion is a closed 'island': points trace the lower boundary (G ~ 1/m_a free-streaming line, low mass 1 MeV down to min ~2e-10 GeV^-1 near 150 MeV) then up the high-mass/trapping right edge (turnover near m_a ~ 510 MeV) back to the top plot frame (~4e-7 GeV^-1, cut off by plot at m_a ~ 114 MeV) rather than a single-valued curve; ordering follows the traced contour. Astrophysical calorimetric bound from the low-energy supernova population, not a statistical CL and not DM-density dependent.
